articles.title: Breaking the Voodoo curse: D’Angelo, Black Messiah, and the perils of perfection
articles.summary: After 14 years of near silence, the savior of soul set the internet on fire last night
articles.body: I heard D’Angelo for the first time at the turn of the new millennium, and like many people, I felt that I had stumbled onto the savior of modern music. His 2000 masterpiece Voodoo was a completely unique mixture of funk, R&B, gospel, and hip-hop: the guiding star of the nascent neo-soul genre. It went to number one on the Billboard charts, sold millions of copies, and won numerous high profile awards. You could be forgiven for asking, “How is he going to top that?” The answer was brutally simple: he didn’t. For the last 14 years D’Angelo has been silent, save a few middling singles and numerous rumors about his health, sanity, and the progress of a follow up. And then, without much warning, it arrived at midnight last night, a 12-track album entitled Black Messiah. For a man whose career essentially missed the modern internet, new music from D’Angelo did not fail to set social media on fire. I feel conflicted about critiquing this record, mostly because I’m just overjoyed that D’Angelo feels comfortable and confident to make and release new music. I’m rooting for him, in other words, in a way that I don’t for most musicians. Voodoo was such a powerful antidote to the stuff that passed for R&B at my high school, hits from teeny boppers like Britney Spears, N’Sync, and 98 Degrees. If I’m being brutally honest, however, Black Messiah doesn’t measure up. The greatest joy of Voodoo was D’Angelo’s vocal range, alternating from silky smooth to ragged gospel to lascivious funk. He plays with that diversity on this new album, but to me his vocals sound far less distinctive and are often buried beneath a layer of distortion that smothers the transcendent sensation I get listening to tracks like Voodoo’s “Untitled (How Does It Feel).” On “How Does It Feel,” D’Angelo’s voice is double- and triple-layered, crafting elegant harmonies with himself. The instrumental backing is minimal, building to a series of crescendos around his aching vocals. It was a rare instance of an artist baring himself completely — both musically and, in the unforgettable video, physically. It made him into a sex symbol and, more than decade later, hasn’t lost any of its power. The video is four and half minutes, but for the real experience, listen to the full album version and wait for that moment six minutes in (Six. Minutes.) when he completely lets loose. All of which is to say, Black Messiah is music that I like. It’s full of live instrumentation, interesting arrangements, and strikingly human vocals that stand out against the majority of singers on the charts and in the clubs these days. There are weird digressions and also tight grooves, but ultimately the new D’Angelo sounds like what it is: the tortured follow-up to an album that cannot be topped, plagued by 14 years of self-doubt from the singular genius at the center of it. On “Back to the Future (Part I),” D’Angelo sings “So if you’re wondering about the shape I’m in / I hope it ain’t my abdomen you’re referring to.” That’s a sly joke about his personal struggles with substance abuse and weight gain, a nice moment where he shows a sense of humor about the demons that have kept him silent for so long. I think that’s why I feel like such a heel for reviewing this album. Every album cannot be a new Voodoo; hell, it’s possible he’ll never reach those highs again. I’m just happy D’Angelo is back, and apparently the rest of the internet is, too. I hope this record, whatever its flaws, means we can expect more new music from him, preferably sooner than 2028.

articles.title: As 'Percy Jackson,' Walker Scobell is fronting one of Disney's biggest shows. A summer job and home far from Hollywood keep him grounded.
articles.summary: "Percy Jackson" star Walker Scobell tells Yahoo about his low-key life away from filming, why he clicks "not interested" on videos of himself and what his po...
articles.body:
Walker Scobell has spent his teen years bringing a demigod to life on Percy Jackson and the Olympians , which returns Nov. 20 for its third season.

Back home, his friends say they can't watch the show because he's in it. He shares a family car. His hair routine? No more than a quick shake of the head. And over the summer, he worked at a local pool, where playing the son of Poseidon didn't give him much authority.

"Nobody really listened to me — ever," he tells Yahoo for our Generation Now series.

That low-key life suits the 17-year-old high school senior just fine. When we connect, he's just arrived home after classes. Here, outside Erie, Pa., Hollywood feels a long way away. So does Camp Half-Blood.

That separation extends to his phone. When a video of himself appears as he scrolls, he quickly clicks "not interested," he says. He doesn't want to become so preoccupied with how he looks that it affects his acting.

Before graduation, there's another teen role on his calendar. He's voicing Glider, Red's son, in The Angry Birds Movie 3 , in theaters Dec. 23.

Here, Scobell unpacks fame, shares his post-graduation plans and politely answers questions about those curls.

You film 'Percy Jackson' in Vancouver, then come home to northwestern Pennsylvania. What do you like about that distance between those worlds?

I honestly love it. There's not any of this kind of "industry" where I live. It's very different from L.A. and New York, where you're always in it. I love coming back here after filming something because it resets you to how the rest of the world is away from those places. I think it gives me almost an edge in a way because this is a very different place.

You spent last summer lifeguarding there with your two siblings. What did you learn?

A lot of the kids were from my neighborhood — kids I've known for years. I've played these games with them. Now I'm a lifeguard, and it's really hard to yell at people for doing things that you were doing last year and getting yelled at for [ laughs ]. I get it, and I don't want to have to yell at them. That's the most difficult part.

You'd think it was a lot more jumping in the water and being a hero and saving people, but it's just a lot of sitting up on a stand and being the bad guy and yelling at kids. Usually, a shift's four or five hours. You have that little pouch with all your stuff in it, a whistle, and you do your rotations in the stand. Sometimes you have to test the water every hour. Sometimes you do swim team.

You're a TV star, and here you are testing the pool water. Does that strike you as funny?

I guess it's a little strange. I kind of loved it, though. It's very grounded. It just makes me feel luckier when I come back to my other job. To be honest, I thought I was going to be up on the stand, and people were going to come up to me asking for pictures. But I think that happened one time the whole summer. It felt like I was in a little bubble all summer, which was nice.

When you return home after filming, do your friends ask about work or catch you up on what you missed?

Really, they're bringing me up to speed. I don't get a ton of questions about that side of it. It's more like I've just been gone and I get caught up on what's been going on here.

My friends can't watch [ Percy Jackson ] because I'm in it, they always say. That might just be an excuse to not have to watch a whole show that's like eight hours. But I enjoy it because I don't have to worry about embarrassing myself and them watching it and making fun of me for it.

I know for sure I'm going to take a gap year. I don't think I'll go to college because I don't totally see a lot of benefits to me going. It's very expensive, and I almost feel like I'm learning so much every day on Percy . If I went, I would go for acting or something like that, but we have such a good acting coach. In a way, it's like I'm going into my fourth year of acting school — if we get to go back for Season 4.

You've talked about worrying during casting that you might get too old to play Percy. How do you feel about that now, three years in, when you actually are older?

To be honest, I was really worried because I thought I would look very different at 17. I thought I'd have a full beard by now, but I don't.

I think there was a lot of reaction online when I had a growth spurt between Seasons 1 and 2. But the funny thing is, I didn't really grow that much. My brother is 15, the age I was in Season 2, and he's 6-foot-1. He's a lot bigger than I am now. I kind of capped off at 5-foot-10.

I don't think I'm going to look a lot older … if we do get to complete the series. What I am worried about is looking really old for maybe The Heroes of Olympus , the second Percy Jackson series. But who knows if I'll even be playing Percy then? It's so far away.

I know you failed your first driving test . I did too, so I think we're in an elite club. Did you buy yourself a car after passing?

The best drivers do. I sort of bought one at the beginning of Season 1 — it was a mix between me and my parents — because we needed a car in Vancouver. When I got old enough to drive, me and my sister shared it. Now she's in college, and it's going to be me and my brother soon. So I never really had to totally buy myself one.

I don't feel it too much in my regular life because they don't treat me like that here. When I go to Brazil, or I'm doing a big event like a Comic Con, that's when I really kind of feel it. But I also don't know any of the people. I guess it would feel different if I knew all these people really well, and then all of them had a crush on me. But I've never met a lot of them, so it's very disconnected.

Every time I get an image of myself on my phone or TikTok, I just hit "not interested" because I don't want it to affect the way that I'm acting. I don't want to start thinking about how I look when I'm acting. That's not the kind of actor that I want to grow into — one that's just focused on how good he looks and his jawline in every shot. That's not what I'm aiming for.

It's a funny visual to imagine you clicking 'not interested' on an image of yourself.

You've grown up alongside 'Percy Jackson' co-stars Leah Sava Jeffries and Aryan Simhadri. How have your friendships changed since the first season?

I think we've all gotten closer to each other. Though we honestly grow closer to each other when we're away from each other because we're all kind of dealing with the same exact thing.

We periodically grow up with each other — I'll grow up with Leah and Aryan for nine months at a time, then I won't see them for a year. We'll all have grown a lot, then come back together and grow more together.

I'm very close to almost every single person on the set. We get to share this very unique experience together, and I don't think we'll ever forget it.

I watched a video of your hairstylist, Jessica Glyn-Jones, doing your hair for the show, curl by curl. How long does it take to get Percy's hair ready?

It changes. Season 1 was a little shorter because my hair wasn't as curly. Between Seasons 1 and 2, it got a lot curlier, so Season 2 took a good 30 to 45 minutes. Season 3 only took 15 minutes because my hair was much shorter. The other thing is, not only does it have to match how it looked the day before, but there are always fans blowing in our faces — and water, humidity and stuff like that. They have to make sure it doesn't move.

What do you do with your hair when you're not working? How do you maintain your curls?

I don't really do anything. I get out of the shower and I shake it out, then it just curls how it does. Right now, this is slept on.

I had really long hair this summer. I don't like having to deal with waking up with one side of my head not curly anymore and the other side really curly. That's what happens when it's longer.

What's weird about my hair is that if I cut the top … it just gets almost straight. It's only the length that makes it curly, in a way. I like to keep it shorter when I'm not working. It's just easier to maintain.

Something else I noticed in that hairstyling video: You weren't on your phone. What's your relationship with your phone like?

I spend so much time with my hairstylists, my makeup artists and stuff like that. It almost feels disrespectful to show up and just stare at my phone, my head down, and not talk to them. I try to make conversation every day. It also makes it easier for them to do their work if I'm listening, turning my head and keeping my head up.

Next season — if we get one — I think I'll be looking at my phone a lot more because I won't have school. That's the big deterrent: I can't use my phone during school, so I rarely look at it when I'm working. I leave it in the green room or the school trailer [and] try to stay away from it.

But it's tempting because sometimes Aryan will come into wherever I'm doing school and just sit and play Clash Royale or games on his phone, and I really want to play with him.

What else do you like to do between scenes?

We're trying to get into card games — like Magic: The Gathering or Dungeons & Dragons . We decided we will next season — if we get one. That's such a good way to pass the time. I also try to read when I can. I read this massive book about Alexander the Great, and I got to do that for school last year. That's another thing I think I'll be doing with the time I'll gain by not having school.

How many Camp Half-Blood shirts do you own?

Two. I took one from set, but I lost it. I lose all my stuff. I still have the one that I got for Christmas in third grade. I also have my Season 3 outfit. I'm not going to take it out of the bag because I don't want to lose anything.

What's the best prop you've been allowed to keep, and what are you still lobbying for?

The coolest thing I got is a metal Riptide, which was a big deal because those are really expensive to make. There are only like two or three of them, and I have one from Season 1. I want to get one from the last season we do — which hopefully hasn't passed — too. Every season, they make Riptide a little bigger to grow with me.

This interview has been edited for length and clarity.

articles.title: Pós-menopausa não é catástrofe, diz escritora Melanie Pérez Arias | G1
articles.standfirst: Em seu primeiro romance, a escritora venezuelana-peruana Melanie Pérez Arias usa a queda inexplicável de cabelo de uma mulher como ponto de partida para explorar identidade, perdas, corpo feminino e amizade.
articles.summary: A escritora Melanie Pérez Arias explora a pós-menopausa e o corpo feminino em um romance que transforma a perda de cabelo em uma jornada de amizade e libertação.
articles.body:
Un Animal que se Deja Caer é o primeiro romance da escritora venezuelano-peruana Melanie Pérez Arias. — Foto: Nolan Rada

Pense por apenas um segundo: o que significa o seu cabelo para você?

Se, algum dia, você o perdesse sem causa aparente , o que estaria disposta a oferecer ou ao que renunciaria para tê-lo de volta?

O cabelo, segundo a escritora venezuelana-peruana Melanie Pérez Arias, de 40 anos, é algo que não sangra, mas dói.

E, no seu primeiro romance Un Animal que se Deja Caer ( Um animal que se deixa cair , em tradução literal), o cabelo é o ponto de partida para toda uma viagem íntima sobre a identidade, perdas, renúncias e, sobretudo, a amizade no universo feminino.

A obra acompanha Miriam, a protagonista, em uma cidade e em paisagens cujos nomes não são identificados. A escolha busca dar universalidade à narrativa, para que qualquer pessoa possa se reconhecer nela: a história de um corpo que falha sem aviso, de um grupo de amigas que representa a família escolhida e dos silêncios, tabus e mitos que ainda cercam o corpo feminino.

Em um livro que é América Latina, mas sobretudo, Caribe (com sincretismo, humor em meio à tragédia e um certo toque de salsa), Pérez Arias também elabora uma magia narrativa, evitando que a história que ela conta toque o presente do seu país de nascimento. E esta, segundo ela, é uma decisão política.

A BBC News Mundo, o serviço em espanhol da BBC, conversou com Melanie Pérez Arias durante o Hay Festival Arequipa, celebrado no Peru entre os dias 5 e 8 de novembro.

Confira os principais trechos da entrevista:

Capa do livro Un Animal que se Deja Caer — Foto: Lumen

BBC News Mundo: Em princípio, o tema do seu livro é o cabelo — o cabelo como identidade.

Melanie Pérez Arias: Sim, mas eu diria até que o tema é uma anedota, o ponto de partida, quando a protagonista começa, um dia, a perder cabelo sem entender o porquê.

Mas, como centro, existem dois temas chave no livro: a amizade, especificamente a amizade feminina, e a identidade, sobre quem somos quando aquilo que acreditávamos que fôssemos não serve mais, porque caducou ou por algum fato sobrenatural e inexplicável. Não sou mais aquilo, então, o que e quem sou eu?

BBC: Como o livro é de ficção, o que há de você nesta busca, nesta mudança de identidade?

Pérez Arias: É um livro sobre a transformação e a busca de identidade que, na minha opinião, são íntimas. Elas ocorrem primeiramente em um espaço muito minúsculo da alma e, a partir dali, podem se refletir externamente.

Mas, para mim, a transformação da identidade, também como escritora mulher e migrante, é sempre uma busca constante, não apenas de quem sou agora, do lugar que ocupo, mas de quais são as pequenas mudanças que vão ocorrendo.

Na sua essência, na sua personalidade, como você se deixa influenciar pelo entorno, como aquilo em que você acreditava ser uma verdade para você, como uma catedral, desmorona e quanta beleza existe nessa destruição do que você era e na construção do novo.

Somos invadidos por relatos sobre mudanças que são muito duros e apocalípticos. Mas, nestas pequenas transformações em que o tempo passa e você logo descobre que, sim, sou a mesma pessoa, mas não sou a mesma, ali, naquele espaço diferente, acho que existe muita beleza.

E andar acompanhados neste processo de mudança é uma grande sorte. No caso de Miriam, que é a protagonista, ela está acompanhada das suas amigas nesta mudança que ela precisa viver.

E, além disso, parte do que eu queria construir nesta personagem era este acompanhamento que ela se dá a si própria, quando começa a refletir de forma muito íntima sobre o que está acontecendo com seu cabelo, mas também com a sua vida, seus amores, suas afeições, seu relacionamento, seu trabalho e até com seu tempo livre.

BBC: O que acontece quando o corpo falha?

Pérez Arias: O corpo toma decisões que não têm muito a ver com a pessoa e, ao mesmo tempo, têm tudo a ver com ela. Nunca sabemos o que acontece com Miriam, mas, para elas, é uma espécie de traição.

Existe toda uma corrente que fala sobre a somatização e como nossos pensamentos influenciam o corpo.

Mas, na realidade, uma das ideias que eu também queria transmitir neste livro é a do corpo como mistério. Vivemos em uma época em que queremos explicar tudo em excesso e entender absolutamente tudo o que acontece em cada uma das nossas células. Mas muitas coisas estão fora do nosso controle.

Para mim, isso revela muito sobre o quanto preciso deixar ir e o quanto preciso aceitar como destino.

BBC: Outro tema que atravessa todo o livro é o da beleza, a ponto de que a protagonista prefere a morte a ficar sem cabelo. Como mulher, como venezuelana, como você viveu essa pressão estética, que chega a este extremo?

Pérez Arias: Tudo isso foi uma viagem também para mim porque, como mulher venezuelana, minha identidade e minha cultura são totalmente marcadas por estas buscas do protótipo de beleza, desde o Miss Venezuela, que tem um peso muito forte sobre nós, mulheres.

Moro no Peru há anos e voltei à Venezuela em 2023. Boa parte dos comentários tinham relação com a minha transformação física: quantos quilos, a mais ou a menos, eu tinha, como estava o meu cabelo, o quanto eu havia envelhecido.

No livro, eu precisava que minha protagonista fosse uma pessoa totalmente trivial, o que dá na mesma para ela, pois, se fosse uma questão de vida ou morte, eu acabaria matando a personagem no final do livro porque o cabelo caiu e ela não conseguiu resistir.

A lenda de María Lionza e a crença religiosa da santería fazem parte do romance — Foto: Thierry Monasse/Corbis via Getty Images

BBC: Sobre o cabelo, você escreve "não é algo que sangra, mas dói".

Pérez Arias: Eu me perguntava por que o cabelo não seria importante.

Por que o cabelo não seria um motivo para sentir luto? Por que perder o cabelo não seria uma razão para sentir luto?

Não é um braço, não é um membro, você não está, na verdade, em risco de morte. Mas tem a ver com você, com sua própria imagem. E perder esta imagem também é um processo que não deveríamos menosprezar.

E está na nossa cultura. Em toda a cultura latina, mas, na Venezuela, existem até livros falando sobre como a imagem da Miss foi meio que transcendental para nossa cultura, para nossa identidade.

Sempre havíamos sido reconhecidos como o país do petróleo, dos jogadores de baseball e das misses. Não é pouca coisa.

No meu caso, parte do processo de transformação da migração é aceitar isso que é identitário de outro olhar, muito mais crítico, mas também com ternura.

BBC: Você dizia inicialmente que a história é sobre amizade, mas concretamente entre mulheres. E é verdade que os homens aparecem pouco ou são muito secundários...

Pérez Arias: Esta é uma história em que o conjunto das mulheres é protagonista, mas digamos que a decisão não foi tão política quanto eu gostaria de admitir.

Eu não pensei "vou deixar os personagens masculinos relegados".

Muitas decisões na literatura têm a ver com o que a história pede e esta exigia uma fraternidade muito feminina, pois tem a ver com descobertas de temas relacionados com o corpo e com a velhice.

E eu precisava que minha protagonista estivesse bem cuidada com o passar do tempo e bem cuidada com estas amigas.

Como mulheres millennials [nascidas entre 1981 e 1996], estamos também atravessando um processo de descentralização da relação romântica e de retirar os homens do centro de tudo o que significa nossa experiência de vida.

Não digo que seja algo exclusivo dos últimos tempos, mas, neste caso, eu precisava que estas amigas estivessem disponíveis para ela, para que a história avançasse.

Além disso, pessoalmente, a amizade é muito importante e sempre digo que não consigo imaginar onde eu estaria agora não fosse pelas minhas amigas. Não consigo imaginar e isso é assustador.

BBC: Existe um momento em que você coloca na boca de uma personagem: "você não é velha, algum romance deve ter". E, em muitas partes do romance, você indica isso, que a mulher de uma certa idade parece não ter direito ao amor, ao desejo e é até mesmo invisível. Por que você quis transmitir isso?

Pérez Arias: Existe um livro que foi muito importante para mim no processo de produção deste romance, que é Sobre os Ossos dos Mortos [Ed. Todavia, 2019], de Olga Tocarzuk, prêmio Nobel [de 2018].

Neste romance, a protagonista é uma mulher na casa dos 50 anos, que começa a cometer crimes, respaldada pelo anonimato de ser uma mulher de certa idade. Este romance fundiu minha mente.

Ainda estou longe deste momento da vida. Mas, na realidade, o que encontro são muitos relatos de mulheres idosas da minha vida que me dizem que esta é uma boa etapa.

Estamos dominadas pelo relato de que, com a pós-menopausa, tudo ficará mal com seu corpo e também de que, no processo da mulher, você não terá apenas desafios físicos, mas também será apagada da face da Terra.

Mas, no meu romance, a resposta é: 'não, ainda estamos aqui, temos direito a um corpo, ao prazer, à exploração, até a nos transformarmos e sermos pessoas totalmente diferentes, com direito a sermos vistas e lidas'.

Temos ainda muitos desafios como mulheres, mas o futuro para as mulheres idosas, na pós-menopausa, não parece catastrófico, mas sim um futuro libertador.

A escritora venezuelano-peruana Melanie Pérez Arias — Foto: Nolan Rada

BBC: Um dos temas presentes neste romance são os tabus referentes à saúde das mulheres. Nós já superamos isso?

Pérez Arias: Existe um ponto importante. Este romance se passa no final dos anos 1990. Ou seja, Miriam, a protagonista, foi criança perto dos anos 1945-50. É outro momento histórico, em que as mulheres ainda recebiam mais comentários como "não tome banho quando estiver menstruada, não ande de bicicleta, não pode, não pode, não pode".

Sim, acredito que, agora, existem avanços, embora ainda sejam primários, muito vinculados às áreas urbanas. Meninas que crescem nos interiores dos países latino-americanos ficam de fora.

Na própria Venezuela, temos um grande problema com tudo o que se refere à saúde menstrual, a saúde sexual para as meninas não existe e não há informação. Existe uma vulnerabilidade muito grande.

Existe mais acesso à educação, à informação e divulgação online, mas não acredito que os mitos, por exemplo, sobre a menstruação estejam totalmente derrubados. Além disso, o corpo feminino continua sendo um mistério.

BBC: Foi uma decisão política fazer com que seu romance se passasse nos anos 1990 e não posteriormente? [Hugo Chávez chegou ao poder na Venezuela em 1998]

Pérez Arias: Foi uma decisão totalmente política que o romance transcorresse até o final dos anos 1990 e, de fato, quase em 1998. Foi uma decisão narrativa porque, se Miriam estivesse no presente, ela entraria no ChatGPT ou no Google, ficaria sabendo por que o cabelo cai e o romance teria 30 páginas.

Mas também foi algo absolutamente consciente e político o fato de deixar de fora tudo o que tivesse relação com a história recente da Venezuela e com o chavismo. Eu não queria que eles aparecessem em nenhum momento, pois já são onipresentes demais na minha história e na história do país para também aparecerem no meu primeiro romance.

BBC: Para quem conhece a Venezuela, o romance é um viagem por muitas paisagens do país, cujos nomes você não menciona, mas que estão ali. Como foi escrever sobre esses lugares estando em Lima, no Peru?

Pérez Arias: O caso é que terminei o romance na Venezuela. Mas, antes, foi interessante escrever sobre um território geográfico sem estar nele e ainda sem mencioná-lo, pois eu não queria que houvesse muitos sinais e nomes.

A saudade nos traz a necessidade de encher de nomes, de renomear, de enfeitar as coisas. A saudade nos traz a necessidade de indicar nossos espaços e recuperar nossa linguagem. Mas eu queria que o romance fosse um espaço mais aberto porque esta é uma história muito mais universal. Eu queria que pessoas de todo o mundo pudessem viajar para esse lugar onde estão as protagonistas.

BBC: Miriam recorre à ciência, recorre às amigas, recorre à santería ...

Pérez Arias: A santería [prática que mescla tradições católicas e o culto aos orixás] está por toda parte. A cultura iorubá, a santería , a religião iorubá está em toda parte. Não só na Venezuela, e faz parte do nosso legado, como países colonizados e como países independentes.

Além disso, recebemos toda a cultura africana através da escravidão. Negá-la ou tentar encobri-la apenas com a religião católica, ou até satanizá-la, é uma pressão existente na cultura caribenha. Mas estas manifestações sempre conseguem encontrar uma forma de encontrar seu curso.

Evidentemente, tudo tem um lado luminoso e um lado obscuro. Mas o que me interessava era que minhas personagens estivessem em contato com o lado luminoso desta religião e desta cultura, até porque a ciência abandona minha protagonista. Ela não entende por que o cabelo dela cai, não consegue respostas.O que faço?

Todas nós passamos, em algum momento, pela ideia de "e se eu ler as cartas? E se lançar os búzios? E se perguntar ao horóscopo?" Porque é normal, é também muito próprio da nossa cultura. E eu queria que fosse retratado de forma muito respeitosa, com muita beleza, do ponto de vista luminoso, porque, obviamente, é também assim que eu vivenciei quando morava na Venezuela. Nesta relação com o mágico, com o misterioso, existe algo tão íntimo e tão profundo que eu não queria deixar de fora do romance.

BBC: O que você quer que as pessoas extraiam do seu romance?

Pérez Arias: Que elas se aproximem do romance com a curiosidade de conhecer estas personagens a quem tenho tanto carinho. São personagens que, para mim, são encantadoras, que talvez eu possa prometer que irão ficar com os leitores por um longo tempo. Eu gostaria que elas abordassem o romance com esta curiosidade.

E algo que eu gostaria que elas levassem consigo ao terminarem de ler é que existem coisas que não saberemos explicar sobre o que faz o nosso corpo, mas o meu desejo é que você tenha no caminho a companhia de personagens e pessoas que amam você e tornem as coisas um pouco mais fáceis para você nesta viagem única de nos descobrirmos como seres humanos: falíveis, com corpos que sofrem coisas, porque acontecem coisas com os corpos.

Neste relato, nesta experiência, desejo que você tenha a companhia de amigas e de pessoas que a apoiem e façam você rir.

Parte do que eu queria era que o romance não fosse um drama insuportável sobre mulheres em crise, à beira de um ataque de nervos, mas sim que fosse uma viagem desafiadora, difícil, na qual se pudesse respirar, onde houvesse ar e que esse ar fosse também marcado pelo humor, pela vontade de rir das nossas tragédias, que é o que há de mais latino-americano.

articles.title: Festival de teatro gratuito em Boa Vista celebra 25 anos da Criart | G1
articles.standfirst: Público poderá assistir as peças 'Cordel do Amor Sem Fim', 'Tiquim' e 'A Formiga Fofoqueira'. Programação celebra os 25 anos da companhia Criart Teatral.
articles.summary: Festival de teatro gratuito em Boa Vista celebra os 25 anos da Criart com drama, palhaçaria e mostra histórica no Teatro Municipal neste sábado e domingo.
articles.body:
Peças da da companhia Criart Teatral, fundada em 2021 em Roraima — Foto: Criart Teatral/Divulgação

A companhia de teatro Criart apresenta três espetáculos gratuitos neste sábado (21) e domingo (22), no Teatro Municipal de Boa Vista . A programação celebra os 25 anos do grupo em Roraima . Os ingressos podem ser retirados na bilheteria uma hora antes de cada sessão.

Com o tema, " Criart 25 Anos: Nossa História em Cena ", o festival tem apresentações que incluem drama, palhaçaria — linguagem teatral que usa humor, improvisação e técnicas de palhaço para contar histórias, e uma montagem infantil. Veja a programação:

" Cordel do Amor Sem Fim " – neste sábado (21), às 20h. O drama contemporâneo acompanha as irmãs Carminha, Madalena e Tereza em uma trama de paixões, desejos e escolhas que também envolvem conflitos familiares. A classificação é para maiores de 14 anos.

" Tiquim " – neste domingo (22), às 16h. A montagem aposta na palhaçaria para contar as confusões de Mulica, Dona Jura, Caramela, Trambolho e Sidó após receberem um convite misterioso.

" A Formiga Fofoqueira " – neste domingo (22), às 19h. A peça apresenta uma história ambientada no campo, com fantasia, realidade e personagens inusitados.

A programação começou nesta sexta-feira (20), com “Clarices”. Inspirada na obra de Clarice Lispector, a montagem combina poesia e performance para abordar identidade, existência e as múltiplas experiências de ser mulher. A sessão ocorre no Teatro Escola.

Além das apresentações, o festival oferece ao público a oportunidade de conhecer um pouco mais da história do Criart Teatral desde a fundação,em 2001. A exposição “ Criart Teatral – 25 Anos ” reúne lembranças de diferentes momentos da trajetória do grupo, com fotografias, lambe-lambe, miniaturas de cenários, peças interativas, troféus e outros objetos.

A mostra fica aberta à visitação até este domingo, no hall do Teatro Escola, no Teatro Municipal.

Fundado pela atriz e diretora Kaline Barroso, em 2001, o Criart construiu uma trajetória dedicada à produção artística, à formação e à democratização do acesso à cultura. Ao longo de 25 anos, desenvolveu espetáculos para diferentes públicos, participou de festivais regionais e nacionais e conquistou reconhecimentos, entre eles o Prêmio Myriam Muniz de Teatro e premiações no Festival de Teatro da Amazônia (Fetam).

Como parte da programação de aniversário, a companhia homenageou pessoas que ajudaram a construir a trajetória do grupo dentro e fora dos palcos, com reconhecimento a artistas, profissionais dos bastidores, parceiros e representantes de instituições culturais.

Foram homenageados Graça Paula, responsável pela confecção de figurinos, e Baronso Lucena, que há anos contribui com a iluminação dos espetáculos. Também receberam reconhecimento Fábio Cavalcante, pela contribuição jornalística e divulgação do trabalho do grupo, e as preparadoras corporal e vocal Alexsandra Paz e Nathália Lago.

A homenagem também contemplou integrantes de grupos parceiros, como Arteatro e Locombia, além de representantes do poder público e de instituições culturais.

articles.standfirst: Shows gratuitos iniciam às 18h, no Bar Caldeira, com apresentações de Bab Lak do Sax, Nunes Filho e outros artistas. A programação segue até 27 de novembro e celebra a cultura dos beiradeiros.
articles.summary: O Festival do Beiradão inicia programação gratuita no Bar Caldeira com shows de Nunes Filho e Bab Lak do Sax para valorizar a música e a identidade do Amazonas.
articles.body:
Festival celebra 'beiradão', estilo musical tradicional do Amazonas — Foto: Divulgação

A segunda edição do Festival do Beiradão do Amazonas começa nesta segunda-feira (23), em Manaus , com shows gratuitos a partir das 18h, no Bar Caldeira, no Centro Histórico. A abertura marca o início de uma programação que segue até 27 de novembro e reúne artistas para celebrar e valorizar a música e a cultura dos beiradeiros.

A programação de lançamento contará com apresentações de Bab Lak do Sax, Kaiza Marques, Nunes Filho, Nayan da Guitarra, Os Kuximawara, Los Matrinxãs, Marcelo Nakamura e Maestro Janjão.

O festival busca fortalecer o beiradão como parte da identidade cultural do Amazonas e ampliar o debate sobre o reconhecimento dessa manifestação como patrimônio cultural.

A iniciativa também pretende destacar a importância de preservar a tradição e criar políticas públicas para manter essa expressão cultural. A segunda edição ainda promove o encontro entre diferentes gerações de artistas, com atividades ligadas à cultura, à economia criativa e à formação.

articles.title: My Hero Academia returns to Crunchyroll with a 105-minute movie featuring Deku, Bakugo and Todoroki
articles.summary: Fans of My Hero Academia had another reason to return to the world of professional heroes and dangerous villains.
articles.body: Fans of My Hero Academia had another reason to return to the world of professional heroes and dangerous villains. The franchise's third theatrical film, World Heroes’ Mission, arrived on Crunchyroll on November 20, 2026, giving viewers another chance to follow Izuku Midoriya, Katsuki Bakugo and Shoto Todoroki beyond their usual school battles. The 105-minute film offered a global threat, a race against time and a new character who played an important role in Deku's journey.My Hero Academia: World Heroes’ Mission brings Deku back to CrunchyrollOriginally released in Japan on August 6, 2021, World Heroes’ Mission was directed by Kenji Nagasaki and produced by Studio BONES. Creator Kohei Horikoshi served as chief supervisor and handled character design, keeping the film connected to the wider anime universe.The story unfolded during the Endeavor Agency arc, but moved the young heroes far beyond the familiar surroundings of U.A. High School. This time, they faced Humarise, an organisation convinced that people with Quirks posed a threat to humanity's future.Led by Flect Turn, the group planned to spread deadly toxins through bombs placed in locations around the world. The threat forced Pro Heroes and students into an international operation to find the devices before they could cause mass destruction.Deku, Bakugo and Todoroki became part of the mission. Their challenge was not simply to defeat another villain. They had to work against a global deadline, with the safety of countless people at stake.The film also introduced Rody Soul, whose connection with Deku added a more personal dimension to the action. Its international setting and focus on teamwork gave the story a different feel from the regular anime episodes.My Hero Academia movie offers Japanese and English versions on CrunchyrollCrunchyroll's November 20 announcement confirmed that the film was available with Japanese audio and English subtitles, as well as an English-dubbed version. It reportedly earned around 3.18 billion yen at the domestic box office by September 2021. Its music also featured contributions from Asian Kung-Fu Generation, whose songs included the theme track "Empathy" and the insert song "Flowers".For longtime followers, the film offered another look at familiar heroes facing a threat on a much larger scale. articles.title: Anthony Clark’s Official Cause Of Death Revealed
articles.summary: An official cause of death for Yes, Dear star Anthony Clark has been reported: The comedian, who passed November 10 at 63, died from septic shock, with influ...
articles.body:
An official cause of death for Yes, Dear star Anthony Clark has been reported: The comedian, who passed November 10 at 63, died from septic shock, with influenza A and chronic alcoholism also included as underlying conditions. Acute kidney failure is added as a significant contributing factor.

The details comes from a death certificate obtained by People magazine late yesterday.

The death of Clark, who started his career as a stand-up comedian and later became the star of TV sitcoms Boston Common and Yes, Dear , was announced earlier this month via a social media post from his Yes, Dear co-star and friend Mike O'Malley. Deadline reported at the time that initial reports indicated his death was connected to complications related to pneumonia and the flu. (Clark's age has been variously reported as 62 and 63).

Clark was best known for starring alongside Mike O'Malley, Jean Louisa Kelly and Liza Snyder on the 2000 CBS sitcom Yes, Dear . Created and executive produced by Greg Garcia and Alan Kirschenbaum, the comedy about two couples living under the same roof ran for six seasons.

On hearing the news of Clark's death, Garcia, who also created NBC's My Name I Earl , shared the following thoughts with Deadline:

I've been very lucky to be friends with some of the funniest people in the world, and Anthony Clark had the most insane sense of humor of all of them. The things that would come out of his mouth were so unexpected and hilarious. Over the last two or three years we had reconnected, and I always looked forward to our monthly phone calls where we would catch up and make each other laugh. Recently, he was so full of joy and encouragement when he found out I was trying stand-up comedy for the first time. He enjoyed talking about the art of stand-up, being on the road, and would also offer some great advice. Just a few weeks ago we were laughing hysterically on the phone, trading jokes and telling stories. It's a sad day, and I'll miss him very much. I'm glad he was able to bring a lot of joy and laughter into the world.

articles.title: Ashton Kutcher on track for billionaire status after ignoring wife Mila Kunis' early tech warnings
articles.summary: Ashton Kutcher's Sound Ventures saw its $435 million Anthropic investment grow to $7 billion after the AI company's stock market debut on Nov. 19.
articles.body: Ashton Kutcher is on his way to becoming a billionaire after going against his wife's advice and investing his money in tech. According to Newsweek, the 48-year-old actor's venture capital firm, Sound Ventures, made a $435 million investment in the artificial intelligence company, Anthropic, in 2023, an investment that is now worth $7 billion. Bloomberg reports that the company owns 0.5 percent of Anthropic, which has an estimated IPO valuation of $1.4 trillion. Anthropic went public on the stock exchange on Thursday, Nov. 19. Kutcher co-founded Sound Ventures in 2015 and since then has invested in a number of successful companies. He previously invested in Spotify, Uber and Airbnb with his investment firm, A-Grade Investments, which he co-founded in 2010. WHO IS DARIO AMODEI, THE ANTHROPIC CEO PUSHING INDEPENDENT AI OVERSIGHT? Kutcher has since relinquished his position as partner at Sound Ventures, but has stayed on as a senior advisor. Although the "Two and a Half Men" actor has found success with his investments, his wife, actress Mila Kunis, wasn't always on board with him investing in certain companies. "Early in our dating, two things came up. He was like, ‘Hey, there’s this company, it’s kind of a rideshare,'" she said on "The Late Show with Stephen Colbert Show" in 2021, referencing his investment in Uber. "He’s like, ‘There’s this company, it’s kind of like a cab company, but anyone can drive the cab.’ I was like, ‘That's the worst idea ever.'" The actor decided to convince Kunis by suggesting she try the service herself, an idea which left her "furious." "He is like let me get you this thing, called Uber, let me order it, you can test it out," she said. "And I was like you are going to put me in a car with a stranger. What is wrong with you? Like I was furious at him." He later approached her about investing in Bitcoin, saying he told her, "I gotta explain this thing to you, tell me if I’m crazy," and then told her about "this thing, mining for money, it’s called cryptocurrency." "I was like, ‘Then who is going to make sure it’s safe?’ He was like, ‘That’s the point,'" she said. "He didn’t listen to me...This happens all the time." When speaking with Business Insider in April 2017, Kutcher admitted he initially passed on Uber when the CEO of the company approached him, but then realized "there was a product market fit there" and immediately called the CEO back. He also admitted to having the same feelings about Airbnb, noting his initial thought was, "Who's going to want a stranger sleeping on their couch?" "Oftentimes the foundation of great companies are extraordinarily counterintuitive where the founders have some data nodes that would suggest that the intuition relative to a certain sector is wrong or that there's some fundamental intuition that is wrong," he explained. "And that we when you unveil that fundamental intuition to be wrong, you actually find an entire pasture of green grass that nobody else is building in because there's a fundamental intuition that is that has been an assumption of so many people for so long that they've never actually built into that sector." "There are companies all the time that he will talk about that to me seem so ludicrous," she said. "Why would I want to sleep on someone's couch and pay for it like it is ludicrous and yet here we are. And I Airbnb everything and Uber everywhere, and I use cryptocurrency, so guess what, I have never been happier to be wrong." Kutcher and Kunis first met when they were both cast on "That '70s Show" when he was 20 years old and she was 14. Although they played love interests on the show, their real-life friendship never crossed the line into romance at the time. They began dating in April 2012 after they reconnected at the Golden Globe Awards in January 2012. Kutcher was previously married to Demi Moore from 2005 to 2011, while Kunis was in a long-term relationship with Macaulay Culkin from 2002 to 2011. articles.title: Vishva Hindu Parishad seeks ban on Ranbir Kapoor's 'Ramayana: Part 1', alleging that, 'the film is an attempt to glorify Ravana, historical events have been fabricated'
articles.summary: The controversy surrounding Ranbir Kapoor and Yash-starrer 'Ramayana' has escalated, with the Vishva Hindu Parishad (VHP) demanding that the film's censor
articles.body: The controversy surrounding Ranbir Kapoor and Yash-starrer 'Ramayana' has escalated, with the Vishva Hindu Parishad (VHP) demanding that the film's censor certificate be revoked and its theatrical screenings stopped. VHP International President Alok Kumar accused the makers of distorting elements of the epic and glorifying Ravana, raising objections to the film's portrayal of several characters and events.VHP general secretary Bajrang Lal Bagra also criticised the film for allegedly deviating from Maharishi Valmiki's original Ramayana, claiming that fabricated incidents have been introduced and important characters omitted. In a statement, he alleged that the film attempts to push a political narrative while hurting the religious sentiments of more than one billion devotees of Lord Ram.Speaking about the objections, Alok Kumar said, “We recently watched and reviewed the film ‘Ramayana’, and we have objections to it. Historical events have been distorted and fabricated incidents have been added. This is not merely an attempt to introduce some dramatic elements to make the film entertaining, it also strikes at the very foundational values on which the story of Ram is based. Lord Ram spent 14 years in the forest, meeting people from all sections of society. He lived in the attire of an ascetic and walked barefoot. In an important act of women’s empowerment, he visited Mata Ahilya’s ashram and restored her dignity and respect. Lord Ram and Bharat also referred to Nishadraj as their friend and treated him as an equal. By establishing a bond of friendship with him, they conveyed the message that there is no distinction between touchable and untouchable or between higher and lower castes what matters is the bond of love. Lord Ram’s conduct towards Kevat was also aimed at establishing social harmony. These are essential elements of the Ramayana, but none of them have been depicted in this film."He further alleged that the film presents Ravana in a favourable light and attempts to elevate his character. “From the very beginning, the film portrays Ravana as a liberator of Dalits, the exploited and the deprived, showing him as someone who works for their welfare. This is also an attempt to glorify Ravana," he added.While the Ramayana has traditionally been narrated through the journey of Lord Ram and Sita and the triumph of good over evil, Namit Malhotra's adaptation has also brought Ravana into the spotlight. Played by Yash, the antagonist has been drawing considerable attention from audiences, with many appreciating his portrayal. The growing admiration for the character, however, appears to have become one of the points of contention for the VHP, which has now called for the film to be withdrawn from theatres.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.title: Quote of the day by Frank Sinatra: ‘I would like to be remembered as a man who had a wonderful time living his life,’ the singer's simple lesson on friendship, family and happiness
articles.summary: Explore Frank Sinatra's heartfelt answer on how he wished to be remembered, focusing on friendships and family rather than awards. Discover the values that shaped his extraordinary life.
articles.body: Frank Sinatra spent decades in the spotlight. Hit songs, a pile of films, an Oscar on the shelf. But when journalist Walter Cronkite asked how he wanted to be remembered, he skipped all of it. He talked about good friends, a fine family and enjoying himself. That was plenty for him.Today's quote reads: "I would like to be remembered as a man who had a wonderful time living his life, and who had good friends, a fine family. I don't think I could ask for anything more than that, actually."He said it to Cronkite in 1965, in a CBS News special about Sinatra that aired in November that year.What does the quote by Frank Sinatra mean?Frank Sinatra had loads he could have pointed to. One of the most recognisable singers of his generation, a successful acting career, audiences all over the world. None of it made his list. Friends, family, and the fact that he'd enjoyed the ride. It's a pretty personal answer. After building that career, he didn't seem bothered about how many awards people would attach to his name.It also nudges you about the stuff you keep putting off. Work, studies, plans for the future, and meanwhile the coffee with a friend, the phone call home or a quiet evening with family keeps sliding to some other day. His answer drags those ordinary things back to the front.How is the quote by Frank Sinatra relevant today?Social media makes it hard not to compare. Everyone's posting new jobs, holidays, houses, milestones. Even when your own life is going fine, you can feel like you should be doing more, or getting there faster.Frank Sinatra's take is a different way to look at it. People you can rely on, time with your family and good memories to look back on won't show up on a list of achievements, but they count.Wanting a successful career is perfectly fine, of course. The trap is telling yourself you'll enjoy life once you hit the next goal, because there's probably always another one behind it. You don't need everything sorted before you spend time with people you care about or enjoy what's going on around you.Early life of Frank SinatraFrancis Albert Sinatra was born on 12 December 1915 in Hoboken, New Jersey, to a family of Italian heritage. He got into music growing up, drawn to big band performances and the singers of the day. He left high school before graduating and went after music.Some of his first big breaks came through bandleaders Harry James and Tommy Dorsey. He sang with their orchestras before going solo.How did Frank Sinatra rise to fame?Frank Sinatra's popularity exploded in the 1940s. Crowds turned up in huge numbers, especially young female fans who became known as "bobby-soxers". The excitement around him was enormous, and he quickly became one of the biggest names in American popular music.Acting worked out for him too. His role in From Here to Eternity won him the Academy Award for Best Supporting Actor in 1954. Songs like "My Way" and "Fly Me to the Moon" became closely tied to his name, and his career ran for decades across music, films and live shows.He left behind a huge body of work, but that 1965 answer to Cronkite shows what he cared about outside of all of it. He wanted to have enjoyed his life, and to be remembered by the people who shared it with him.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.title: California's film industry faces uphill battle as Trump steps in and East Coast rivals gain ground
articles.summary: President Trump's "Make Hollywood Great Again" push comes as Hollywood faces declining production, with New Jersey emerging as a "savvy" competitor with uncapped film tax credits.
articles.body: LOS ANGELES — California's entertainment industry continues to face mounting challenges even as Washington steps up efforts to keep film and television production in the United States and President Donald Trump launches a campaign to "Make Hollywood Great Again." Fox News Digital spoke with industry experts to assess the state of Hollywood and examine the mounting pressures on the industry, including intensifying competition from the East Coast. Hollywood runaway production gets White House spotlight "Hollywood doesn’t mean Hollywood anymore. Hollywood is empty," Trump said at a rally in October. "It's not without a lot of truth, unfortunately," entertainment lawyer Jonathan Handel told Fox News Digital. HOLLYWOOD JOBS FLEE OVERSEAS AS CONGRESS SCRAMBLES TO STOP PRODUCTION EXODUS — WITH TRUMP'S BLESSING In recent weeks, President Trump has signaled a new focus on keeping film and television production in the U.S., after years of productions moving overseas in search of lower costs and more lucrative tax incentives. "Hollywood, and so many other places, have been virtually ‘emptied out’ by the Tax Incentives, and much more, given by other Countries. Everyone feels strongly about the Motion Picture and Television Industry — and so do I, and we all want to save it. It was MADE IN AMERICA, and must STAY IN AMERICA," Trump wrote in a post to Truth Social last week. The commander-in-chief said he is working with senators across the aisle, including his longtime political adversary Sen. Adam Schiff, D-Calif., on the Motion Picture, Television, and Entertainment Revitalization Act, legislation aimed at bringing the entertainment industry back to the U.S. The push comes as industry experts warn that production is leaving California for competing states and countries at an alarming rate. Shoot days in California are down roughly 40% since 2023, according to data from FilmLA. PELOSI, OMAR JOIN TRUMP AND SCHIFF AS UNLIKELY ALLIANCE PUSHES TO ONSHORE KEY INDUSTRY "It would have been easier to keep this production in Los Angeles than it is to claw it back," Handel said. One significant disadvantage for California is the structure of its tax incentive program, production experts told Fox News Digital. The Golden State’s tax credit is currently capped at $750 million, though California Gov. Gavin Newsom has recently proposed expanding it to at least a $1 billion. Fox News Digital reached out to Gov. Newsom for comment. Meanwhile, states like Georgia offer uncapped credits, while states such as New York and New Jersey offer larger or more flexible incentive structures, allowing productions to access incentives without competing for a limited pool of funding, making them more financially attractive to major studios. "For many, many years, this industry was in California and New York for the most part. And then we saw Canada get into the incentive business. And then, we saw many countries start to build out their own incentive structure. And the truth is, they work," Stagerunner founder and CEO Jason Fisher told Fox News Digital. HOLLYWOOD FEELING MORE HOPEFUL AMID A PUSH FOR FILM TAX CREDITS AND PARAMOUNT STAYING PUT, FILMMAKER SAYS "It's cheaper to go elsewhere," he added. The bipartisan Motion Picture, Television, and Entertainment Revitalization Act, backed by Trump, would create a 20% federal production incentive for films. "There is a movement now and legislation introduced to create a national incentive," Handel said, noting that Ireland and other countries already have national incentives. "That would stack on top of state incentives, whether California, whether Georgia, New Jersey, New York … and is really what's necessary to make production competitive again in California and in the United States," he added. The White House told Fox News Digital in a statement that the Trump administration wants to "Make Hollywood Great Again" and that it is committed to ensuring Hollywood remains a "powerful source of American culture." NETFLIX CHIEF ADMITS TRUMP IS HELPING SHOWBIZ INDUSTRY AS FEDERAL TAX CREDIT BILL AIMS TO FUEL HOLLYWOOD JOBS New Jersey emerges as a rival to California’s moviemaking industry Even with renewed federal attention on domestic production, California faces a separate challenge: competing with other states for film and television projects. A federal incentive could help bring production back from overseas, but it would not eliminate California's disadvantage against states offering more generous tax credits. One of the Golden State's most aggressive competitors is New Jersey, which has attracted major investments from some of Hollywood's biggest players. "They've been a very savvy and very aggressive competitor," Handel said. Netflix, Lionsgate and Skydance are among the entertainment giants investing in New Jersey, where production spending has surged from roughly $67 million to more than $1 billion in less than a decade. Industry experts told Fox News Digital that the state's "aggressive" tax incentives have been a major draw for studios. "They have a 35 percent rebate, perhaps one of the most generous in the country," Fisher told Fox News Digital. "And it also includes above the line. So, it is about as competitive as it gets." NEWSOM DENIES PRESSURING CALIFORNIA AG INTO PARAMOUNT SETTLEMENT AFTER LIBERAL BACKLASH "Netflix is building a studio, Lionsgate’s building a studio, 1888 is another studio being built there," he added. "There’s a lot of infrastructure." Fisher also pointed to California's lengthy and complicated application process as a factor discouraging studios from filming in the state. "Filling out the application process in California, it is a gigantic hassle," said the former production executive. "And it's an application. You aren't guaranteed acceptance." He said states with uncapped tax incentives offer producers greater certainty when planning projects, making them more attractive for producers. "When there's no cap, you don't have to fill out an application and be accepted. They're not choosing which projects to give the incentive to … and that makes it a lot easier for producers," he added. ROB RIGGLE SAYS HOLLYWOOD WORK IS DISAPPEARING FROM LA: 'IT'S THE EXCEPTION NOW' Handel said California's limited pool of tax credits makes it increasingly difficult for the state to compete with jurisdictions offering productions more generous, uncapped incentives. "When you're competing against … uncapped incentives in New Jersey, Georgia, and the European countries, it's not enough," the entertainment lawyer said. As other states offered increasingly competitive incentives, studios began investing in permanent production infrastructure in New Jersey, New Mexico, Texas and Georgia, further shifting the industry's center of gravity away from California. "As we saw those incentive programs grow, then we saw infrastructure build out. We saw companies building sound stages, we saw a local crew workforce training happening," Fisher told Fox News Digital. articles.title: Ty Pennington calls out 'excessive' home renovation trend people do in kitchens
articles.summary: Ty Pennington calls renovation trend overkill, while sharing why kitchens and baths still build equity.
articles.body: Ty Pennington has built and maintained a successful career with his extreme home makeovers, but there's one renovation trend he believes homeowners are taking a little too far these days. In an exclusive interview with Fox News Digital, Pennington — who has recently partnered with Insmed on the "Suspect BE" campaign to encourage people with unresolved respiratory symptoms to pursue further testing — weighed in on where homeowners should and shouldn't put their renovation budgets, calling out oversized kitchen islands packed with redundant appliances as a trend that has crossed into overkill. "I would probably say the island with three dishwashers," the veteran HGTV star, 62, said when asked about renovation trends that go overboard. "It's maybe a little excessive. This is coming from somebody who was a personal dishwasher for many years of my life." JOANNA GAINES REVEALS WHY SHE AND CHIP WALKED AWAY FROM 'FIXER UPPER' AT THE HEIGHT OF ITS SUCCESS "There is a point that you almost get too big," he continued. "Is there an island that's almost the size of a small court? Possible. So I think sometimes we may be sort of outgrowing things. We may be just going too big. I know that's hard to believe, but I think sometimes we've got to scale back not only in budget, but also maybe in size. Cozy is cool." While Pennington advocates for dialing back the scale, he still acknowledges that kitchens and bathrooms remain the smartest investments for homeowners looking to build equity. "The most expensive are the kitchens and the bathrooms, but I do think they're kind of necessary if you plan on selling, because that's what people look at first," he explained. "If somebody is passionate about a certain project that they know exactly what they think they want it to look like, sometimes you have to just use a different room in a different project. We don't always agree on everything. I don't think that happens in any aspect of life. What I try and do is lend my perspective and also throw out a couple of crazy ideas that hopefully sometimes lead to something sort of midway between." "When you're dealing with a spouse and their plans, you sort of have to just be like, well, you just have to trust," he added. "And I think that's the key." These days, Pennington is splitting his time between his home in Georgia with Merrell and his mother’s home in Florida, where he has stepped into a caretaker role. Nearly 20 years ago, his mother was officially diagnosed with bronchiectasis, or BE—a chronic, progressive lung condition that causes permanent widening and scarring of the airways. Pennington, who has partnered with biopharmaceutical company Insmed as a spokesperson to raise awareness and educate others about BE, said his mother's diagnosis—combined with his own past health scare involving a life-threatening throat abscess—fundamentally shifted his perspective on life. articles.body:
Sarah Michelle Gellar and Freddie Prinze Jr.'s daughter Charlotte Grace Prinze, 17, wants to become an actor.

While attending the People and InStyle F1 Drive-By Party in Las Vegas on November 20, Gellar revealed that Charlotte is taking acting classes with the same acting coach who trained her and Freddie at the start of their careers.

During the event, Freddie and their 14-year-old son Rocky James Prinze, an aspiring F1 driver, also competed in a race.

Sarah Michelle Gellar and Freddie Prinze Jr. 's kids have their sights set on two ambitious career paths. On November 20, Gellar attended the People and InStyle Drive-By Party ahead of the F1 Grand Prix of Las Vegas. Her daughter Charlotte Grace Prinze , 17, accompanied her while Freddie and their son Rocky James Prinze, 14, competed in a race.

Speaking with People at the event, Gellar said, "Yes, of course," when asked if Charlotte had inherited her parents' acting bug. The Buffy the Vampire Slayer star added that the teenager is taking "acting classes weekly." "She takes acting classes with the coach that Freddie and I ... that we started with," the mom of two explained.

Happy to discuss her passion for acting, Charlotte chimed in, "It's my favorite thing. I'm so excited, and I can't wait to start hopefully soon."

The ultra-rare F1 outing marks Charlotte's first red carpet appearance with either of her parents. When asked whether she was nervous about the event, the 17-year-old replied, "I was before, but I'm excited now."

For the outing, the mother-daughter duo twinned in coordinated little black dresses and matching mini purses. Gellar's look consisted of a shimmering, sleeveless minidress paired with semi-sheer tights, diamond earrings, and pointed-toe heels. The I Know What You Did Last Summer actress completed the ensemble by styling her mid-length blonde hair in waves.

Charlotte, meanwhile, opted for a micromini under an edgy black leather jacket, which she paired with tights and black boots. Like her mom, she accessorized with a tiny black purse and wore her long, dark hair down in waves. The teenager was last seen publicly with Gellar at the September 2022 screening of Do Revenge in Los Angeles.

Gellar and Freddie's son Rocky also has high career aspirations. "Rocky is racing, and he had a race this weekend, so he couldn't come," Gellar told People at the F1 event. "So we're representing here, and Freddie and Rocky are at his race." Recently, Freddie shared a photo of Rocky driving a Porsche on Instagram.

articles.title: Who will be Robert Pattinson's 'Bond girl' - and does the role need to change?
articles.summary: Speculation is rife as to who will play the new 007's leading lady, with commentators saying she will need a "very strong identity".
articles.body:
After months of speculation, we finally have a new Bond. The question now is - who will play Robert Pattinson's leading lady?

What's clear is that Pattinson's announcement as 007 has completely upped the game.

He's one of Hollywood's biggest stars, so all eyes are on Amazon MGM to see whether they go for an equally big name as a 'Bond girl', or if they'll take a chance on someone a little less well known.

Whoever is cast opposite him, though, needs to have a "very strong identity of her own", believes film critic Larushka Ivan-Zadeh - "someone distinctive, sexy, complicated".

Showbiz reporter Catrina Rose agrees: "I'd love to see a Bond girl who's just as interesting and unpredictable as he is."

And then, some say the whole concept of a Bond girl is outdated and the role needs to evolve for a new era. So what can we expect?

No actress has yet confirmed they're in the running - but stars who have been bandied about the internet include Zendaya , whose name shot to the top of the list after Pattinson's casting.

The duo have already shared three films together this year and make a "really exciting pairing," says Ivan-Zadeh.

Rose agrees that as one of the most recognisable actresses in Hollywood, Zendaya is "definitely someone I'd be thinking about now".

But her Euphoria co-stars Hunter Schafer and Sydney Sweeney could give her a run for her money.

There have been rumours about Sweeney getting the role for months, and you can see why, says Dr Llewella Chapman, a film historian at the University of East Anglia. "She has sex appeal and an ability to take on tougher roles too," she tells the BBC.

Sweeney was given a boost last month by former Bond girl Trina Parks, who told the Telegraph she would fit the role well because Bond needed a woman with "ownership over her sexuality".

Speculation is also growing over Pattinson's partner, actor and singer Suki Waterhouse . She once said she'd love to play " a bad-ass Bond girl ".

But there isn't a precedent for husband-wife couples in the films, and it may be more likely that she picks up a cameo role, if indeed she wants to.

Meanwhile, TV presenter Maya Jama has picked up new interest following her storming run on Celebrity Traitors. After she quit Love Island , rumours swirled that she could be the next Bond girl - but she's just signed a Netflix deal, so it's unclear whether that would still be a possibility.

Another strong contender is Florence Pugh who, like Zendaya, also stars alongside Pattinson in Dune: Part Three. Earlier this week she threw her hat in the ring to be in the new Bond film - although as a villain, rather than his leading lady.

"She ticks quite a few boxes if they're looking for someone bankable," says Rose. "I could absolutely see her as a Bond woman who turns out to be the villain, someone Bond thinks is on his side, but she's actually been playing him the whole time."

Queen's Gambit star Anya Taylor-Joy is another name Amazon MGM could be thinking about if they want a big, recognisable actress, as well as Killing Eve's Jodie Comer (Villanelle meets Bond, anyone?)

Meanwhile, Crazy Rich Asians star Gemma Chan told Variety she was "flattered" by fans speculating she could be a Bond girl. "Absolutely I would," she said .

Other names that have been floated include Saoirse Ronan, Margaret Qualley, Marisa Abela, Emily Blunt, Lily James, Chase Infiniti, Inde Navarrette, Simone Ashley, Deva Cassel and Ambika Mod .

And it could easily be someone totally different. Producers have previously chosen a Bond girl who isn't particularly famous yet - or is on the cusp of stardom.

But then there's the wider question of whether the whole idea of a "Bond girl" is now somewhat outdated.

Historically, the character had little agency and existed primarily as Bond's romantic interest - and the term "girl" itself is also criticised for infantilising women.

Monica Bellucci rejected the label. She told the Guardian ahead of her appearance in Spectre in 2015: "I can't say I'm a Bond girl because I'm too mature to be a Bond girl. I say Bond lady; Bond woman."

The way the films have treated Bond girls "hasn't always aged well", says Rose.

Some scenes from 1960s Bond films are "basically rape", and "wouldn't fly today", said No Time To Die director Cary Fukunaga in 2021 - referring to Thunderball and Goldfinger.

In reality, we have come a long way since then.

Over the years, producers have taken steps to usher the franchise into the modern era.

These days, the women of Bond are now much more likely to be sharp, capable equals to 007 - and what's defined as "attractive" has also evolved.

Belluci's inclusion in Spectre as a "Bond woman" aged 50 was widely praised for spotlighting a different type of sex appeal (even though she was only four years older than Daniel Craig in real life).

We've also had other powerful women in Bond, such as Michelle Yeoh's Colonel Wai Lin and Lashana Lynch's MI6 agent Nomi, who also made history as the first black female 007 .

Rather than fitting the traditional Bond girl mould, both of them were competent women who could give Bond a run for his money.

"We've moved away from the role being someone with a silly name and for Bond to pat on their bottom," says film critic Ivan-Zadeh. "It's moving in the right direction".

Many people say, however, there is still further to go.

Having more female Bond villains, as well as love interests, could be one way to make it more equal, suggests Rose. "That's what I'd want to see."

"They can be romantic interests, villains, spies, allies or even the person who ultimately outsmarts Bond. There's room for all of those roles," agrees showbiz journalist Nikki Onafuye.

Another way the roles could evolve is by bringing in "a queer or sexually fluid Bond woman," suggests Ivan-Zadeh. "Someone whose desires don't simply revolve around Bond. That would create some genuinely interesting chemistry."

Others are hoping to see more diverse actresses cast from film markets such as China, India or Nigeria.

"There have been a number of women of colour in the past, but I'd like to see more," says Be Manzini, writer and filmmaker.

"I'd like to see an Indian Bond girl," agrees Chapman. "Aishwarya Rai was touted for the follow up to Die Another Day but never got there."

More broadly, there is an appetite to see Bond girls have their own lives.

"For me, it's about giving these women proper storylines," says Onafuye. "They should have their own motivations and their own ambitions."

None of this is to say we should do away with the traditional Bond glamour.

"No-one wants to see Bond girls slumping around in their PJs," says Ivan-Zadeh.

But the important distinction is that "being sexy shouldn't be the only thing a female character has to offer," says Onafuye.

"To those arguing that it's fine for Bond's women just to be sexy and hot, I'd say there's nothing sexier or hotter than a woman (or man) with a brain and a wit," adds entertainment journalist Caroline Frost.

Ultimately, whatever direction the new producers go in, most agree the "Bond girl" or Bond woman is a key part of the Bond universe.

But continuing to evolve is crucial, says Chapman. "It's about retaining the humour and history of Bond but also recognising - this is 2026."

There are, of course, lots of other women within the films, and for Frost, the key is to have a range of different Bond women on screen, "all well matched with 007 in terms of strength, resources and, above all, wit".

"Bond has always had fascinating women," agrees Rose. "I'd just love the next film to give them the space to be as interesting as the man in the tuxedo."

articles.title: Priscila Tossan programa para 2027 o álbum 'Onze', produzido por Iuri Rio Branco com 'sonoridades diferentes' | G1
articles.body:
Priscila Tossan lança na quarta-feira, 25 de novembro, o single '.com', amostra inicial do álbum 'Onze', previsto para ser lançado no primeiro semestre de 2027 — Foto: Divulgação

♬ Descontados os feats em singles de artistas como Rafael Mike e Wado, a cantora e compositora Priscila Tossan não apresenta há três anos um lançamento fonográfico da própria artista. O último single solo de Tossan saiu em novembro de 2023 com a regravação de “A beleza é você, menina” (Bebeto e Rubens Francisco Alves, 1979), música da fase áurea do cantor Bebeto.

O hiato na discografia solo da artista carioca se encerra na próxima quarta-feira, 25 de novembro, com a edição do single “.com”, amostra inicial do álbum que Tossan planeja lançar no primeiro semestre de 2027.

O álbum se chama “Onze”, tem produção musical de Iuri Rio Branco e gera um segundo single em janeiro, um funk. Inspirado no ciclo de renovação do sol, símbolo central da identidade visual do álbum, “Onze” versa sobre transformação, liberdade e a possibilidade de recomeçar sem deixar para trás quem se é.

“Estou testando muita coisa, explorando sonoridades diferentes e me jogando em vários campos”, adianta a artista, revelação da sétima edição do programa “The Voice Brasil”, exibida pela TV Globo em 2018.

“Onze” é o terceiro álbum de Priscila Tossan, mas o primeiro feito por vias independentes, após o encerramento do vínculo contratual da cantora com a Universal Music, gravadora pela qual a artista lançou os álbuns “Iceberg” (2020) e “Live” (2021), além de EPs como “Cuca fresca” (2022). Até por isso o álbum “Onze” é caracterizado como o disco do “renascimento artístico” de Tossan, movimento iniciado em 25 de novembro com a edição do single “.com”, gravado pela cantora com participações de Gavi e Vitão.

articles.title: Anitta usou biojoias de designer de SP no álbum EQUILIBRIVM | G1
articles.standfirst: Peças usadas por cantora foram feitas com matéria-prima natural. Álbum também foi indicado ao Grammy 2027 na categoria de Melhor Álbum de Música Global.
articles.summary: Anitta utilizou peças sustentáveis do designer Alan Malves em EQUILIBRIVM, álbum que rendeu seu primeiro Grammy Latino e indicação ao Grammy 2027.
articles.body:
A cantora Anitta usou biojoias produzidas por um estilista e designer de Santa Bárbara d'Oeste (SP), no interior de São Paulo, durante as gravações do álbum 'EQUILIBRIVM', que venceu o Grammy Latino e foi indicado ao Grammy 2027 na categoria de Melhor Álbum de Música Global.

Lançado em abril de 2026, o projeto apostou em referências de vários gêneros tradicionais brasileiros e na espiritualidade relacionada a religiões de matriz africana.

As peças foram feitas por Alan Malves. À EPTV , afiliada da TV Globo, ele explicou como as biojoias chegaram ao conhecimento da equipe de Anitta.

"Meu trabalho foi chamado para fazer parte de um projeto na Casa de Brígida. A partir dessa parceria, surgiu esse interesse por parte dos produtores da Anitta. Produtores que cuidam do vestuário, dos visuais da Anitta, procuraram esse espaço, Casa de Brígida, e pegaram as minhas peças para serem usadas."

Anitta em imagens de 'Equilibrivm' — Foto: Divulgação

Malves destaca que a cantora já usou cerca de 12 peças produzidas por ele, em ambas as partes do álbum premiado.

"Depois disso, eles continuaram procurando tanto a Casa de Brígida como o meu ateliê que troca minhas peças, que a gente enviou inúmeras peças para eles, e ao todo já a Anitta usou 12 peças, tanto na primeira parte de 'EQUILIBRIVM' quanto na segunda parte."

Ao explicar o que são as biojoias, o estilista cita ser o responsável por toda a produção das peças feitas por ele, inclusive a coleta.

"São acessórios sustentáveis, ecológicas, feitas com matéria-prima natural, vindas da nossa natureza brasileira. Eu utilizo cascas, sementes, flores, frutos, pedras naturais, fibras, uma gama gigantesca de pesquisa, de trabalho, tanto de coleta, quando eu coleto materiais naturais aqui na região onde eu moro e também materiais que vêm de várias partes do Brasil."

Além de Anitta, outros artistas brasileiros já usaram os itens de Malves, conta o estilista.

"Meu trabalho já esteve em desfile em revista, em jornais, em exposições, já esteve usado por vários artistas brasileiros, como a Anitta, mas também o cantor Mestrinho, a atriz Paolla Oliveira, já esteve na TV Cultura, na TV Globo, uma das últimas peças foi usada pela cantora Fafá de Belém."

Após 12 indicações ao longo de mais de uma década sem levar o troféu para casa, Anitta finalmente conquistou o primeiro Grammy Latino da carreira, no último dia 12 de novembro. A estrela pop venceu a categoria Melhor Álbum de Pop Contemporâneo em Língua Portuguesa com "EQUILIBRIVM".

Na edição de 2026, Anitta chegou a Las Vegas concorrendo em duas frentes: Melhor Álbum de Pop Contemporâneo em Língua Portuguesa e Álbum do Ano, categoria principal da noite na qual figurou como a única representante brasileira.

Até levantar o gramofone dourado, a relação de Anitta com a Academia Latina da Gravação foi marcada por presença constante nas listas de finalistas, mas sem vitórias.

Boa parte de suas nomeações anteriores ficou nas categorias urbanas e gerais. Há pelo menos cinco anos, Anitta vem focando em uma estratégia de internacionalização de sua carreira, o que a colocou em disputa direta com os maiores nomes do mercado hispânico.

Anitta recebe o prêmio de Melhor Álbum Pop Contemporâneo em Língua Portuguesa por "Equilibrivm" durante a 27ª edição do Grammy Latino , em Las Vegas, Nevada — Foto: REUTERS

Anitta também foi indicada ao Grammy 2027 na categoria de Melhor Álbum de Música Global. O anúncio foi feito pela Academia no dia 16 de novembro.

Ela concorre com Davido ("Oriadé"), Angélique Kidjo ("Hope!!"), Ayra Starr ("Starrgirle") e Tems ("Love is a Kingdom"). A premiação do Grammy 2027 acontece no dia 7 de fevereiro de 2027, em Los Angeles, nos Estados Unidos.

Após a indicação, Anitta fez uma série de vídeos nos stories do Instagram para celebrar o feito:

"Não fiz álbum pensando nisso", afirmou a cantora, ao relatar sua reação durante a produção do disco ao ser impulsionada por uma amiga a pensar na premiação. "Eu falava: Que mané Grammy o quê? Troca o disco. Vamos pensar no público, nas pessoas, na população ouvindo. Mas agora estou achando uma delícia, um tesão, tudo."
